userStories.title: Add oscillation state primitives
acceptanceCriteria: When `recordOscillations` and `getOscillations` are imported from the `src/execution` barrel, then both values are callable functions.
When `getOscillations(store, "US-9")` is called with a fresh `Map`, then it returns `0`.
When `recordOscillations(store, "US-1", 2)` is called, then it returns `2`.
When `recordOscillations(store, "US-1", 2)` has run, then `getOscillations(store, "US-1")` returns `2`.
Given `recordOscillations(store, "US-1", 1)` has run, when `recordOscillations(store, "US-1", 2)` is called, then it returns `3`.
Given `recordOscillations(store, "A", 2)`, `recordOscillations(store, "B", 5)`, and `recordOscillations(store, "A", 1)` run in that order, then `getOscillations(store, "A")` returns `3`.
Given `recordOscillations(store, "A", 2)`, `recordOscillations(store, "B", 5)`, and `recordOscillations(store, "A", 1)` run in that order, then `getOscillations(store, "B")` returns `5`.
When `createRuntime` creates a fresh `NaxRuntime`, then `rectificationOscillations` is a `Map` with size `0`.
When a config omits `review.conflictDetection`, then parsed `config.review.conflictDetection.enabled` is `true`.
When a config omits `review.conflictDetection`, then parsed `config.review.conflictDetection.maxOscillations` is `2`.
When a config sets `review.conflictDetection.maxOscillations` to `4`, then parsed `config.review.conflictDetection.maxOscillations` is `4`.

routing.reasoning: A small additive state/config feature spans four production modules and several established test seams, but follows existing synchronous Map and Zod-default patterns.

userStories.title: Wire the rectification oscillation circuit-breaker
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record source-agnostic regressed-different-source iterations and pause a blocking rectification-exhausted story once its configured cumulative threshold is reached.

**Motivation** — When it happens, the story escalates tier-by-tier (`powerful → balanced → powerful → …`) and re-runs the whole story each time, re-hitting the identical wall and burning cost while the operator sees only a silent money-drain.

**Approach** — Increment site — `src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts`, after the `runFixCycle` call (`rectification.ts:319`) returns `cycleResult`. Count `cycleResult.iterations` whose `outcome === "regressed-different-source"` and, if > 0, call `recordOscillations(ctx.runtime.rectificationOscillations, ctx.storyId, count)`. `ctx.runtime` is the stable run-scoped instance threaded through every per-attempt `PipelineContext` rebuild (same access pattern as `run-phase.ts`), so the count accumulates across escalation attempts. `runRectification` receives `CallContext`, whose concrete story key is `ctx.storyId`; this is the codebase-correct form of the spec’s story identifier.

**Approach** — Halt decision — `src/execution/post-run.ts`, in `decideStageAction`, inside the existing "Rectification exhausted with unfixed findings" branch that today returns `{ action: "escalate", reason: exhaustedReason }` (the block ending ~`post-run.ts:411`). Before escalating, read the cumulative count and config; if the breaker is enabled and `count >= maxOscillations`, mirror the existing `needsHumanReview` direct-pause path (`post-run.ts:467-487`) — send a `notify` interaction via `ctx.interaction?.send({ … })` and return `{ action: "pause", reason }` instead of escalating.

**Approach** — Why the pause route (not a new `FailureCategory`). Returning `{ action: "pause" }` is the same `StageAction` the `needsHumanReview` path already uses (`post-run.ts:487`); it rides the existing `pipeline-result-handler.ts` `case "pause"` → `markStoryPaused` (`src/prd/index.ts:370`) → `story:paused` event → TUI badge / reporters / next-run resume prompt (`paused-story-prompts.ts`). This means the breaker adds no new `StoryStatus` value and touches neither `satisfies never` guard (`resolveMaxAttemptsOutcome` at `tier-escalation.ts:112`, `routeTddFailure` at `execution-helpers.ts:123`) — those stay untouched.

**Approach** — Failure handling: Fail-open on missing config / runtime. If `conflictDetection.enabled` is false, or the runtime counter is absent, `decideStageAction` behaves exactly as today (escalate) — the breaker is a pure addition gated behind a default-on flag; disabling restores current behavior byte-for-byte. Interaction send failure is non-fatal. As in the `needsHumanReview` path, a throw from `ctx.interaction.send` is caught and logged (`logger.warn`); the pause still returns. The pause does not depend on interaction delivery. No false-positive on normal progress. A single `regressed-different-source` iteration is a benign source handoff (e.g. lint resolved → typecheck surfaced) and must never halt; the threshold is `>= maxOscillations` (default 2).

**Scope** — In: a focused outcome-count helper, runtime-counter increment immediately after the fix cycle, and enabled/threshold-gated pause routing for blocking exhaustion. Out: changing `classifyOutcome` or `IterationOutcome`, dedicated interaction triggers, run-end advisory summaries, reviewer AC-grounding filters, new failure categories/statuses, or retry/tier-resolution guards.

**Interface** — Consume US-001’s exported signatures unchanged:

```ts
export function recordOscillations(
  store: Map<string, number>, storyId: string, delta: number,
): number

export function getOscillations(
  store: Map<string, number>, storyId: string,
): number
```

US-002’s test must drive the halt path and prove the pause is produced from the accumulated count returned by `getOscillations`.
acceptanceCriteria: When the outcome-count helper receives `iterations` with outcomes `["regressed-different-source", "partial", "regressed-different-source"]`, then it returns `2`.
When the outcome-count helper receives `iterations` with no `"regressed-different-source"` outcome, then it returns `0`.

When a rectification cycle result contains one `regressed-different-source` iteration, then `getOscillations(ctx.runtime.rectificationOscillations, ctx.storyId)` increases by exactly `1` after the rectification increment site runs.

Given rectification is exhausted with unfixed blocking findings, `review.conflictDetection.enabled` is `true`, `maxOscillations` is `2`, and the accumulated count is `2`, when `decideStageAction` runs, then it returns `action === "pause"`.
Given the circuit-breaker pause result at count `2`, when `decideStageAction` returns it, then its `reason` contains `2`.
Given the circuit-breaker pause result at count `2`, when `decideStageAction` returns it, then its `reason` contains a case-insensitive `oscillat` substring.
Given rectification is exhausted with the same blocking findings and count `1` below `maxOscillations` `2`, when `decideStageAction` runs, then it returns `action === "escalate"`.

Given rectification is exhausted with the same blocking findings and count `2`, when `review.conflictDetection.enabled` is `false` and `decideStageAction` runs, then it returns `action === "escalate"`.
Given rectification is exhausted with blocking findings and `ctx.runtime.rectificationOscillations` is absent, when `decideStageAction` runs, then it returns `action === "escalate"`.
Given rectification is exhausted with a normal single-source unfixable finding and oscillation count `0`, when `decideStageAction` runs, then it returns `action === "escalate"`.
Given the breaker returns `action === "pause"` and an injected interaction channel, when `decideStageAction` runs, then the interaction channel receives a request with `type === "notify"`.
Given the breaker threshold is met and the injected interaction channel throws, when `decideStageAction` runs, then it still returns `action === "pause"`.

routing.reasoning: The change is limited to counting an existing iteration outcome and one existing exhaustion route, with established runtime, configuration, and interaction seams; focused unit/integration-style tests can exercise all branches in one TDD session.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to the existing TypeScript/Bun execution pipeline, not a greenfield build. The rectification signal already exists: `classifyOutcome` records `Iteration.outcome`, and `runRectification` receives the completed `FixCycleResult` immediately after `runFixCycle` at `src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts:319`. The increment belongs there so one stable `ctx.runtime` Map survives reconstructed per-attempt pipeline contexts and therefore accumulates across tier escalations. The live `runRectification` signature receives `CallContext`, which exposes `ctx.storyId`; despite the prose spec’s `ctx.story.id` shorthand, implementation and tests must use `ctx.storyId`. The halt seam is `decideStageAction` at `src/execution/post-run.ts:336`: its rectification-exhausted branch first preserves the existing advisory-only and mechanical-only continue exits, then currently cleans up and returns `escalate` for blocking, non-mechanical findings. The breaker must run only in that latter branch, preserving TDD rollback routing and all non-oscillating behavior. Its pause must reuse the existing best-effort notify shape used by `pauseReason` and `needsHumanReview`, because `StageAction.pause` already propagates through the pipeline result handler to paused-story state, events, TUI/reporters, and resume prompts.

`NaxRuntime` already owns comparable run-scoped per-story state via `adversarialIterations` in `src/runtime/index.ts:133`, initialized beside `quarantineMemo` at `src/runtime/index.ts:254`; add the new Map there with no special close teardown. `src/review/adversarial-iteration-store.ts` demonstrates the small synchronous Map-store convention. The new execution-owned store must be barrel-exported from `src/execution/index.ts`; it has no I/O or await boundary, so JS event-loop mutation is sufficient and story IDs isolate parallel workers. `ReviewConfigSchema` in `src/config/schemas-review.ts:181` already places `review.adversarial` after shared review settings, and `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema.recurrenceDemotion` at `src/config/schemas-review.ts:101` is the exact nested-default pattern to mirror for the new sibling `review.conflictDetection`. Schema-derived `DEFAULT_CONFIG` means no hand-maintained defaults migration is required.

Primary existing tests to extend are `test/unit/runtime/runtime.test.ts` for freshly-created runtime state, `test/unit/config/schemas-review.test.ts` for default/override parsing, `test/unit/execution/rectification-overrides.test.ts` for a focused `runRectification` seam, and `test/unit/execution/post-run-inspection-exhaustion.test.ts` for the blocking exhaustion routing. Use the project’s existing dependency seams (`_storyOrchestratorDeps.runFixCycle`, `makeTestContext`, and `_postRunDeps`) rather than real agent sessions. Compatibility risk is accidentally pausing advisory, mechanical-only, disabled, sub-threshold, missing-runtime, or TDD-isolation outcomes; order the new check after the existing blocking/mechanical gates and make it fail open when config/runtime state is unavailable. No persisted data, external API, StoryStatus, FailureCategory, migration, or cleanup is needed; disabling `review.conflictDetection` restores the present escalation path.
